name: Cervical Dermoid Cyst

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Cervical Dermoid Cyst

criteria.description: Presence of a painless, slow-growing, midline or lateral neck mass on physical examination
Imaging (ultrasound, CT, or MRI) showing a well-circumscribed cystic lesion with heterogeneous internal contents including fat and calcifications
Histopathological confirmation demonstrating cyst lined by stratified squamous epithelium with adnexal structures such as hair follicles, sebaceous glands, and keratin debris
No signs of acute infection or abscess formation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of a characteristic neck mass with supportive imaging findings and histopathological confirmation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical and radiological, confirmed by histopathology after excision.

laboratory: Usually normal laboratory tests unless secondary infection present

MRI revealing heterogeneous cystic mass with fat and keratin components

distinguishingFeatures: Typically located laterally along anterior border of sternocleidomastoid
Lacks internal fat or calcifications on imaging
Midline neck mass that moves with swallowing or tongue protrusion
Absence of fat or calcifications on imaging

redFlags: Rapid increase in size of neck mass
Signs of infection such as erythema, warmth, or fever
